findings.reason: a node implementing "reads no plan file's bytes" finds the second pass already opens none, so it either passes on unchanged code or, if it repairs what the pass really pays (the footprint's `_record_files` listing and per-plan stat), lands a different change than the section authorises.
findings.text: §39's Why states "That check reads every plan document in the project on each pass, whether or not any plan has changed", but at the base revision the owed pass is gated on `owed_plan_review_footprint` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:4801`, landed as `aebadaba56` on 18 November), which reads one `path.stat()` per plan plus the stored records' names and never a document's bytes; `owed_plan_review_pass_due` (`:4868`) skips the pass outright when that footprint is unchanged, and when the pass does run it weighs at most one plan (`PLAN_REVIEW_PASS_LIMIT = 1`, `:4104`) and answers a plan it has already weighed from `_PLAN_FACTS` "without opening the file" (`:4450`). The 23 November profile's remaining per-pass cost is therefore the footprint's stat-per-plan and its full listing of the review store, not plan reads — the same shape of defect as the earlier `s37` finding, where the cited cost was not the stated one.

findings.reason: an unreproducible base arm leaves the node with no negative control and no measurable delta, so the done-when is not satisfiable as written.
findings.text: §39's negative control asserts that at the base revision "every plan file [is] opened on the second pass", which the base cannot exhibit for the reason above, so the control fails to reproduce. It matters because the rubric requires a control that shows the guard firing: a node running its base arm will observe the same zero-or-one reads as its head arm and have no evidence its change did anything. The control needs restating against what the base actually spends (the per-plan stat count and the review-store name listing taken on every sweep), as `s37`'s control was restated.

findings.reason: the declaration and the record disagree, and the new status is what makes the plan depend on an unrecorded claim; either the landing record is written or the declaration is restored.
findings.text: §38 is declared `done` in `plan-section-declarations` while carrying no landing record: its three comments are a run report (`...s38`) and two reviews, and unlike `s35` and `s37` there is no `c-close-s38` naming what landed or linking its evidence, so a later reader cannot tell from the plan what §38 shipped or where to check it. §36 sits beside it with a landed run and a review but remains `implementable`, so the two neighbouring sections present the same evidence shape under opposite declarations.

findings.reason: the run's own directory already holds the log and the node contract requires the capture line, so the omission costs a reader the reconciliation rather than sending the node anywhere wrong.
findings.text: §39 and §40 (plan.html:253, 260) each require a base arm "against a base arm run on `all_debug`" without naming where that arm's log lives or that it must carry the arm's revision, literal command and a closing `EXIT=` line, while §35–§38 each end their done-when with exactly that sentence. A node following §39 or §40 as written can satisfy its base-arm requirement with a log a later reviewer cannot reconcile with the head arm.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `s39` and `s40` cite no file, section or commit, so no anchor is unresolved; the two `href`s added to `_document` (`/reckon/evidence/archive/a-read-costs-what-changed-landed.html#a-read-costs-what-changed-s35`) resolve as the archive page plus an anchor.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — both nodes name a measurable test file, a base arm run on `all_debug`, and a declared negative control; the defect in `s39`'s control is that it cannot reproduce at the base, recorded under `reasoning`.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: a finding — `s38` is declared `done` with no landing record, and `s39`/`s40` name no durable log for their base arms.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the two new test filenames and the plan text carry no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or changelog prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — `s39`'s root cause does not match what the base revision does, and its negative control therefore cannot reproduce.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — `s39` delivers one bound (no plan bytes read on an unchanged pass) and `s40` one (the producer defers to a fresh station sweep); neither carries a second deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `plan-section-depends-on` declares no entry for `s39` or `s40`, and neither waits on another section: `s39` narrows what one owed-review pass reads (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py`) and `s40` narrows which sessions the producer's sweep reaches (`reckon/crew/runs.py`), so no missing dependency exists.
